# tectonic-91260041: the Tectonic TONIC/USD feed as an exhibit

Fixture bundle `tectonic-91260041.tar.gz`: `crossfoot run family --config
config/tectonic-cronos.json` at Cronos block 91,260,041 (2026-09-02), rounds
swept with eth_getLogs from block 90,800,000 (2026-08-29) because no explorer
API serves Cronos, getters read at the pinned block through an RPC with
recent state, every round resolved from its transaction through the owner
contract's Multicall3 aggregate3. The feed is guard-less: one poster key, no
deviation bound, no minimum or maximum, no interval, no maximum age. On the
canonical chain the series shows ordinary posts about every 29 minutes, the
last pre-rollback post at 12:19:37 UTC on 2026-08-30, then nothing until
14:51:46 UTC on 2026-08-31: the SILENCE finding of 26.5 hours. The attack
blocks of 2026-08-30 were discarded by the chain rollback and are not
readable; the three inflated posts MASTR reconstructed are absent from
every read here.

## What this exhibit says and does not say

The verdict of the research page (`wiki/cronos-incident-2026.md`, section
"Would Crossfoot have detected or prevented this?"), quoted verbatim:

No, and it must not claim otherwise. In detail:

- Prevention: impossible by construction. Crossfoot is read-only, post hoc, pinned-block. The decisive window was 10 minutes 29 seconds (first inflated feed post 12:39:10, drain 12:49:39), and the money left in one transaction.
- Detection by its existing checks: none fires. The Tectonic feed is structurally in Crossfoot's family (an owner-posted AggregatorV3-shaped feed, one key, a batching contract in front of it, exactly the "one on-chain key" shape of the Midas customFeeds), but it has no rule to replay. There is no guarded setter and no unchecked setter, only updatePrice; no maxAnswerDeviation, no min or max, no interval. ADMIN_GUARD_BYPASSED cannot fire because there was no guard to bypass. OBSERVED_DEVIATION cannot fire because no published rule was broken: the documented behaviour ("twice hourly or on a 1 percent change") is a trigger, and the feed did exactly that, faster. The mTBILL-style consistency checks (cadence, monotonicity, drift against a contractual benchmark, supply identity) have no benchmark for a governance token. The honest verdict class for TONIC under the current vocabulary is INPUT_GAP with the annotation "no on-chain posting rule exists".
- What it would have seen, descriptively, at a pinned block after the fact: a feed with one poster key, no bound, a 6.46x post followed by 13.4x and 2.26x posts five minutes apart, then 26.5 hours of silence. All true, none of it a rule violation, and all of it in discarded blocks on the canonical chain, which is itself a finding Crossfoot's evidence bundle would surface (a bundle built at 14:00 UTC on Aug 30 would not replay against the chain of Aug 31: SOURCE_STALE at the block, since the pinned block hash no longer exists).

What the bundle shows is the structural finding (no on-chain rule, one
key) and the silence, at pinned blocks, after the fact. The row words are
the guard-less family's: verdict CONSISTENT (no published rule was broken),
posting_path ATTRIBUTED, consumer_action ALLOW with the decision table's
row 11a note that the decision rests on the poster key, and a SILENCE
finding a consumer policy can gate on. None of it is a detection of the
exploit, and the demo must not present it as one.
